neighbours.label: Pay or price noun used as the modifier of a compound that names a limit or adjustment: salary cap, pay cut, wage increase, price premium, signing bonus, hiring freeze (fires on the modifier, before the head noun)
fire: The league voted to raise the salary cap by five percent next season.
Nurses in the region won a wage increase after a short strike.
The airline asked its pilots to accept a pay cut during the downturn.
Fair-trade coffee usually sells at a price premium in supermarkets.
The striker was given a signing bonus when he joined the club.
The university imposed a hiring freeze until the end of the year.
Several clubs are close to the salary cap and cannot add players.
The union rejected the pay freeze proposed by the government.
quiet: The league voted to raise the number of teams by two next season.
Nurses in the region earn a low wage for long hours.
The airline asked its pilots to pay for their own uniforms.
Fair-trade coffee usually sells for a higher price in supermarkets.
The striker was signing shirts when he joined the party.
The university is hiring ten new lecturers before the end of the year.
Several clubs are close to the stadium and share a car park.
The union rejected the timetable proposed by the government.

notes: Card: ' salary' (cap), ' pay' (cut), ' price' (premium), ' signing', but also ' oxygen' (content), ' fitness'. Probes: salary cap 0.49, price premium 0.40, wage increase 0.39, signing bonus 0.39, hiring freeze 0.34, pay cut 0.24; 'The salary was paid' 0.26, 'price of oil' 0.13, 'oxygen content' 0.02, verb 'pay' 0.004. Partly a ' salary'-token effect.
